answer: Each identity registers one grove plot at a distinct vertex of a canyon transect, locking a 75-credit bond to its key and paying a filing fee. The first filing costs 28 credits; the kth costs 28+7(k-1), so the 1000th costs 7021 and 1000 fake identities pay 3,524,500 in fees plus 75,000 locked. An auditor revisits the vertex, re-measures slope and canopy, and recomputes canyon runoff from the grove table; a mismatch burns the bond. A rented-vertex ring fails because bond, measurements, and revisit must match one key. An honest agent registers one plot, pays 28 once, and recovers the bond.
